title: Same-commit desktop vs on-device replay digest across four rounds, including both boss samples and the full-board round
closes: README C4 acceptance item 3 - desktop/Android digest parity.
A4 acceptance - a screenshot of an actual battle, not just the language page.
Director D0/D5/D6 - the on-device presentation metrics those rows list as pending.
verdict: PASS on digest parity for all four rounds (1, 5, 20, 21) - every field identical between desktop and device at the same commit. Round 20 additionally surfaced a presentation defect that is NOT platform-specific; it has since been fixed and gated - see defect_found.

how_the_device_entry_point_was_found.probe_1_scene_override: FAILED - passing res://tools/battle_presentation_baseline.tscn as a positional argument is ignored in an exported build; the game booted normally.
how_the_device_entry_point_was_found.probe_2_intent_extra: FAILED - `am start --esa command_line` never reaches Godot. Same APK: 53 godot log lines with no arguments, 52 with --verbose. The exported entry point is GodotAppLauncher; the real GodotApp is not exported (am start on it raises SecurityException) and the launcher drops the extras.
how_the_device_entry_point_was_found.probe_2_was_first_measured_wrong: An earlier probe counted `grep -c 'godot'` over unfiltered logcat and saw 250 -> 1035 lines with --verbose, and concluded the extra worked. Most of those lines were the framework logging the package name com.godot.game. Filtering by tag (logcat -s godot) showed 53 vs 52. One APK export was wasted on that mistake. Counting occurrences of a word that appears everywhere is not a measurement.
how_the_device_entry_point_was_found.probe_3_cl_asset: assets/_cl_ does ship in the APK, but it is baked at export time and changing it would require re-signing.
how_the_device_entry_point_was_found.chosen: A trigger file. `adb shell run-as <pkg>` writes user://device_harness.json, then the app is launched normally. run-as is available on the Debug build.
how_the_device_entry_point_was_found.trigger_is_one_shot: DeviceHarness deletes the trigger before running, not after. A crash mid-run would otherwise hijack every subsequent normal launch, and the player would find the game replaced by a diagnostic scene that never finishes.

why_an_autoload_instead_of_editing_main: scenes/main/Main.gd is a colleague's active file (D2, the PrepScreen split). A diagnostic entry point is not worth a merge conflict there. The cost is that Main._ready() still runs once before the scene swap, which starts the VFX warmup - and the warmup is parented to root, so it survives the swap. Left running it would compile shaders and stream from flash while the baseline measures exactly those two things, so VFXWarmup.start() now returns early when the harness has claimed the launch.

completion_signal.was: polling logcat for the recorder's completion line
completion_signal.problem: this device emits a CompositionEngine line every ~16 ms; the ring buffer overflows within minutes. On the first run every Godot log line had been evicted, which made 'never started' and 'ran but invisible' indistinguishable.
completion_signal.now: poll for files/battle_presentation_baseline/manifest.json via run-as. It is the last thing the recorder writes and nothing can evict it. logcat is still archived, but filtered with -s godot.

measured.note: Digests are compared; performance is not. Frame rate and memory legitimately differ between platforms - that is not an inconsistency. Both sides ran quality tier MEDIUM.
measured.shader_cache_caveat: The device had a populated files/shader_cache from earlier launches, so these are warm-cache numbers, not first-install numbers.
measured.leaks: peak_orphans is 0 on both sides - the presentation layer frees everything it pools, on device as well.

screenshot_check: The blue bubbles around most units are the shield effect, confirmed by the project owner. The desktop capture of the same replay frame (D6_battle_presentation_cleanup_20260819/baseline_regression/round_01/mid.png) shows them identically, so nothing about them is Android-specific.
not_done: Store and prep-screen screenshots: those need the prep UI driven, which is exactly the D2 territory a colleague is working in.
Low-end device and two-device online acceptance.

rounds_covered.20: boss round at full board - 18 enemies, the heaviest case, and the one with summons
rounds_covered.21: full board, no boss - matches the round B4 used for its tier stress run

defect_found.what: Round 20 drops 3 death cues with reason missing_actor:source. The recorder therefore reports passed=false for that round.
defect_found.who: enemy_mirror_1 / enemy_mirror_2 / enemy_mirror_3 - the copies boss_mirror_lord summons during the fight.
defect_found.not_a_boss_round_problem: Round 5 (a different boss) and round 21 (no boss) both drop zero. The common factor is a summoned unit that respawns under the same uid, not the presence of a boss.
defect_found.not_android_specific: missing_actor_drop_count is exactly 3 on BOTH desktop and device for round 20. The drop is deterministic and reproduces identically on each platform.
defect_found.scope_is_narrow: Only death is affected. The mirrors' other cues play fine: of 77 events sourced from a mirror, attack_start 25, impact 25 and hit_number 19 all played; 3 of 8 mirror deaths were dropped.
defect_found.mechanism_candidate: BattleRenderer.detach_actor_for_death() removes the actor from the prune list but deliberately keeps it registered, which is why an ordinary death plays. BattleVfx.cue_claim_corpses() skips a uid it already holds (`_cue_corpses.has(uid)`), and a mirror dies repeatedly under one uid, so a re-claim can be skipped; if the prune loop then reaches that uid first it calls unregister_actor(), and the Director's _resolve_cue() finds no source actor and drops. Confirming the exact ordering needs instrumentation, not more static reading.
defect_found.impact: The three mirrors vanish instead of playing a death animation - checklist section 6 says a unit must never just disappear.
defect_found.root_cause_found_by_instrumentation: The first hypothesis (cue_claim_corpses skipping a re-claim) was wrong: probes showed the claim at tick 40 SUCCEEDED and the cue was still dropped. The decisive probe line was at release time - held_null=false, held_is_mine=false - the registry already held a DIFFERENT actor for that uid. release_death_actor() unregistered by uid unconditionally, so finishing the old corpse evicted the freshly respawned mirror from the registry, and that mirror's own later death then resolved to no source actor.
defect_found.fix: Added UnitActorRegistry.unregister_if_holds(uid, actor), which erases only when the registry still holds that exact actor; release_death_actor() now uses it. The rule lives in the registry rather than in the caller because a caller cannot see who the registry currently holds and can only guess by uid - the registry can see it.
defect_found.verification: Round 20 missing_actor_drop_count 3 -> 0 and passed=true; rounds 1/2/5/20/21 all zero drops; the two frozen D0 hashes are byte-identical to the D6 evidence and replay_sha is unchanged, so only presentation moved; D2's death_cancel_queue assertion still passes - that is the assertion an earlier guess-driven change in this area broke and had to be reverted wholesale.
defect_found.regression_gate: battle_presentation_director_check grew from 82 to 89 checks, asserting directly on UnitActorRegistry that releasing a stale corpse must not unregister a uid a respawn has taken over. Verified red by putting the bug back - respawn_release_stale and respawn_actor_evicted - and green again after restoring.

ambient_merge_note: budget_merged_ambient and anchor degradation counts legitimately differ between platforms (round 20: 126 desktop vs 295 device) - that is the priority budget shedding more ambient work on the slower device, which is what it exists to do. Digests are unaffected.
evidence_layout: round_01 keeps the full start/mid/end screenshot set; rounds 5/20/21 keep mid.png only, to hold the directory near the size of the existing D5/D6 evidence dirs. The complete sets stay under build/.

device_verified_after_fixes.verdict: PASS - device recorder passed=true with zero failures; round 20 missing_actor drops 0 on both sides.
device_verified_after_fixes.why_this_run_matters: The summoned-unit defects only reproduce when replay playback has to catch up, which never happens on desktop (replay_frame advances by at most 1 per rendered frame there). A green desktop run proves nothing about them, so the device run is the only real evidence.

second_defect_found_and_fixed.what: Round 20 still dropped 2 cues on device after the first fix - attack_start from enemy_mirror_1/2 at tick 15, the tick the mirrors are summoned. Desktop dropped 0.
second_defect_found_and_fixed.my_earlier_claim_was_wrong: I had said the first fix was platform-independent and would surely be 0 on device. It went 3 -> 2, not to 0. An inference is not a measurement.
second_defect_found_and_fixed.mechanism_proven_from_existing_data: frame_performance.csv already held the answer, so no instrumentation was needed: replay_frame advances by at most 1 per rendered frame on desktop (916 zeros, 231 ones) but by 2 (26x) and 3 (2x) on device, where round 20 runs at 9 fps. When playback catches up, _apply_replay_frame() enqueues every skipped tick before _refresh_visuals() builds any models, so a unit summoned inside that batch has no actor when its first cue resolves.
second_defect_found_and_fixed.fix: _spawn_actors_for_tick() now runs before enqueue_tick(), symmetric with the existing cue_claim_corpses(): one holds back the bodies that are about to die so _refresh_visuals() cannot free them first, the other builds the bodies that were just born so they exist at all. Both say the same thing - the renderer must be ready before the Director schedules the tick.
second_defect_found_and_fixed.regression_gate: battle_presentation_director_check 89 -> 93 checks, asserting both calls appear before enqueue_tick in BattleScreen.gd. Source-order rather than behavioural, because the bug only appears when playback catches up and desktop never does - a behavioural test would be green either way.
second_defect_found_and_fixed.the_gate_was_itself_a_false_green_at_fir: The first version searched for "_spawn_actors_for_tick(", which matches the function definition earlier in the file, so moving the call after enqueue_tick still passed. Caught only by putting the bug back and seeing no red. Matching the full call expression fixed it, verified red then green.

cold_cache_measurement.why: Every earlier device number was taken with a populated files/shader_cache, which is not what a player sees after installing.
cold_cache_measurement.how: tools/android_baseline.sh --cold-cache clears files/shader_cache via run-as and verifies it is gone before launching.
cold_cache_measurement.conclusion: First launch is measurably slower. Quote device frame rates with the cache state attached or the numbers look like drift.

new_metrics.particles: Godot 4 has no particle monitor, so the recorder walks the scene tree every 6 frames and keeps the peak: emitting particle nodes, and the sum of their amount (what B4's particle_count_for scales). First version walked from _screen and read 0 for every round - VFXManager parents effects to get_tree().current_scene, a sibling of _screen. A metric that always reads zero is worse than no metric.
new_metrics.result_page: Asserts the Director has no blocking cues the first time the result overlay becomes visible. The drain has a 3 s cap, and past the cap the overlay appears anyway, covering cues that had not finished. Zero occurrences across every round measured.
